claim: Calcium is an essential cellular messenger that regulates numerous functions in living organisms.
source: Calcium is an essential cellular messenger that regulates numerous functions in living organisms.
evidence: This is a well-established fact in cell biology supported by extensive scientific literature.

claim: Salsa6f is a fusion of GCaMP6f and tdTomato optimized for cell tracking while monitoring cytosolic Ca2+.
source: Here, we describe development and characterization of 'Salsa6f', a fusion of GCaMP6f and tdTomato optimized for cell tracking while monitoring cytosolic Ca2+
evidence: The manuscript describes the development and characterization of this novel probe.

claim: A transgenic Ca2+ reporter mouse was created with Salsa6f targeted to the Rosa26 locus for Cre-dependent expression in specific cell types.
source: and a transgenic Ca2+ reporter mouse with Salsa6f targeted to the Rosa26 locus for Cre-dependent expression in specific cell types.
evidence: The manuscript describes the generation of this transgenic mouse line with experimental validation.

claim: The development and function of T cells was unaffected in Cd4-Salsa6f mice.
source: The development and function of T cells was unaffected in Cd4-Salsa6f mice.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing normal T cell development, proliferation, and differentiation.

claim: Salsa6f reports Ca2+ signals during T cell receptor activation in naive T cells, helper Th17 T cells and regulatory T cells.
source: We describe Ca2+ signals reported by Salsa6f during T cell receptor activation in naive T cells, helper Th17 T cells and regulatory T cells
evidence: The manuscript presents experimental data showing Ca2+ signals in these different T cell subsets.

claim: Salsa6f reports Ca2+ signals mediated in T cells by an activator of mechanosensitive Piezo1 channels.
source: and Ca2+ signals mediated in T cells by an activator of mechanosensitive Piezo1 channels.
evidence: The manuscript presents experimental data showing Ca2+ responses to Yoda1, a Piezo1 activator.

claim: Transgenic expression of Salsa6f enables ratiometric imaging of Ca2+ signals in complex tissue environments found in vivo.
source: Transgenic expression of Salsa6f enables ratiometric imaging of Ca2+ signals in complex tissue environments found in vivo.
evidence: The manuscript demonstrates ratiometric imaging in lymph nodes in vivo.

claim: Two-photon imaging of migrating T cells in the steady-state lymph node revealed both cell-wide and localized sub-cellular Ca2+ transients ('sparkles') as cells migrate.
source: Two-photon imaging of migrating T cells in the steady-state lymph node revealed both cell-wide and localized sub-cellular Ca2+ transients ('sparkles') as cells migrate.
evidence: The manuscript presents two-photon imaging data showing these Ca2+ signals in lymph nodes.

claim: Synthetic small molecule Ca2+ indicators such as fura-2 and fluo-4 have greatly expanded understanding of Ca2+ signaling dynamics.
source: Through the use of synthetic small molecule Ca2+ indicators such as fura-2 and fluo-4, imaging studies have greatly expanded our understanding of Ca2+ signaling dynamics (Tsien et al., 1982; Grynkiewicz et al., 1985).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to foundational papers in the field.

claim: Small molecule Ca2+ indicators cannot be targeted to specific subcellular compartments or cell populations.
source: However, such indicators cannot be targeted to specific subcellular compartments or cell populations
evidence: This is a known limitation of small molecule indicators based on their chemical properties.

claim: Small molecule Ca2+ indicators are unsuitable for long-term studies due to leakage out of cells.
source: and are unsuitable for long-term studies due to leakage out of cells.
evidence: This is a well-known limitation of small molecule indicators.

claim: Small molecule Ca2+ indicators often do not faithfully report pure cytosolic Ca2+ signals because of diffusion into cellular compartments such as the nucleus.
source: Moreover, they often do not faithfully report pure cytosolic Ca2+ signals, because of diffusion into cellular compartments such as the nucleus.
evidence: This is a known limitation based on the diffusion properties of small molecules.

claim: Genetically encoded Ca2+ indicators (GECIs) were first developed two decades ago as FRET-based fluorescence probes.
source: One alternative to overcoming these limitations is with genetically encoded Ca2+ indicators (GECIs), first developed two decades ago as FRET-based fluorescence probes (Miyawaki et al., 1997; Romoser et al., 1997; Pérez Koldenkova and Nagai, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to the original papers describing GECIs.

claim: GECIs can be genetically targeted to specific cell types or subcellular organelles.
source: Key advantages to GECIs include the capability for genetic targeting to specific cell types or subcellular organelles
evidence: This is a fundamental property of genetically encoded probes.

claim: GECIs can measure local Ca2+ levels by direct fusion to a protein of interest.
source: measuring local Ca2+ levels by direct fusion to a protein of interest
evidence: This is a known capability of genetically encoded probes.

claim: GECI expression levels can be modulated by inclusion of an inducible promoter.
source: modulation of expression levels by inclusion of an inducible promoter
evidence: This is a standard genetic engineering approach.

claim: GECIs enable long-term studies due to continuous expression of the genetic indicator.
source: and long-term studies due to continuous expression of the genetic indicator (Miyawaki et al., 1997; Pérez Koldenkova and Nagai, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations and is a known advantage of genetically encoded probes.

claim: Initial FRET-based GECI probes were not widely used because their performance fell far behind small molecule Ca2+ indicators in Ca2+ sensitivity, brightness, and dynamic range.
source: Despite these inherent advantages, the initial FRET-based GECI probes were not widely used as their performance fell far behind small molecule Ca2+ indicators, particularly in Ca2+ sensitivity, brightness, and dynamic range.
evidence: This is a historical observation about early GECI development.

claim: Successive rounds of design have resulted in numerous variants of GECIs with high dynamic range and dramatically improved performance.
source: Since then, successive rounds of design and contributions from multiple research groups have resulted in numerous variants of GECIs with high dynamic range and dramatically improved performance (Baird et al., 1999; Nakai et al., 2001; Tian et al., 2009; Zhao et al., 2011; Akerboom et al., 2012; Akerboom et al., 2013; Chen et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to papers describing improved GECIs.

claim: Single fluorescent protein-based GECIs containing a circularly permutated green fluorescent protein (GFP) exhibit high brightness, fast response kinetics, and offer multiple color variants.
source: Single fluorescent protein-based GECIs containing a circularly permutated green fluorescent protein (GFP) exhibit high brightness, fast response kinetics, and offer multiple color variants, including the GECO and the GCaMP series (Tian et al., 2009; Zhao et al., 2011; Akerboom et al., 2012; Chen et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to papers describing these GECI families.

claim: The latest generation of GECIs have crossed key performance thresholds previously set by small-molecule indicators.
source: The latest generation of GECIs have crossed key performance thresholds previously set by small-molecule indicators, enabling GECIs to be widely applied in diverse Ca2+ imaging studies without sacrificing performance.
evidence: This is a general statement about the state of GECI development supported by the literature.

claim: Members of the GCaMP6 family are capable of tracking cytosolic Ca2+ changes from single neuronal action potentials, with higher sensitivity than small-molecule indicators such as OGB-1.
source: Members of the GCaMP6 family are capable of tracking cytosolic Ca2+ changes from single neuronal action potentials, with higher sensitivity than small-molecule indicators such as OGB-1 (Chen et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to the GCaMP6 paper.

claim: Multicolored variants in the GECO family and the RCaMP series allow for simultaneous measurement of Ca2+ dynamics in different cell populations or different subcellular compartments.
source: The availability of multicolored variants in the GECO family and the RCaMP series allowed for simultaneous measurement of Ca2+ dynamics in different cell populations in the same preparation, or in different subcellular compartments within the same cell (Zhao et al., 2011; Akerboom et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to papers describing these multicolored GECIs.

claim: GECI variants can be integrated with optogenetics to simultaneously evoke channel rhodopsin activity while monitoring localized Ca2+ responses in independent spectral channels.
source: These variants can be integrated with optogenetics to simultaneously evoke channel rhodopsin activity while monitoring localized Ca2+ responses in independent spectral channels (Akerboom et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a paper demonstrating this capability.

claim: Individual GECIs can be tagged onto membrane Ca2+ channels to directly measure Ca2+ influx through the target channel of interest.
source: Moreover, individual GECIs can be tagged onto membrane Ca2+ channels to directly measure Ca2+ influx through the target channel of interest, enabling optical recording of single channel activity without the need for technique-intensive patch clamping (Dynes et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a paper demonstrating this approach.

claim: Several GECI-expressing transgenic mouse lines have been reported, many using older variants of GECIs expressed only in selected tissues.
source: Although several GECI-expressing transgenic mouse lines have already been reported, many of these studies used older variants of GECIs that are expressed only in selected tissues (Hasan et al., 2004; Ji et al., 2004; Tallini et al., 2006; Heim et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to papers describing earlier transgenic GECI mouse lines.

claim: The Ai38 mouse line combines GCaMP3 with a Cre/lox system for selective expression in specific cell populations.
source: The Ai38 mouse line overcomes these issues by combining GCaMP3 with a robust and flexible Cre/lox system for selective expression in specific cell populations (Zariwala et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to the paper describing the Ai38 mouse line.

claim: The Ai38 mouse line contains GCaMP3 targeted to the Rosa26 locus but requires Cre recombinase for expression.
source: Based on a series of Cre-responder lines designed for characterization of the whole mouse brain (Madisen et al., 2010), the Ai38 mouse line contains GCaMP3 targeted to the Rosa26 locus but requires Cre recombinase for expression.
evidence: This is supported by citations describing the Ai38 mouse line design.

claim: By crossing Ai38 with various Cre mouse lines, GCaMP3 can be selectively expressed in specific cell populations.
source: By crossing Ai38 with various Cre mouse lines, GCaMP3 can be selectively expressed in specific cell populations.
evidence: This is a logical consequence of the Cre/lox system design.

claim: Target cells in Ai38 mice may be endogenously labeled without invasive procedures, avoiding potential off-target side effects reported in GECI transgenic lines with global expression.
source: Thus, target cells may be endogenously labeled without invasive procedures, avoiding potential off-target side effects reported in GECI transgenic lines with global expression (Direnberger et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a paper reporting side effects of global GECI expression.

claim: The PC::G5-tdT mouse line targets a Cre-dependent GCaMP5G-IRES-tdTomato transgenic cassette to the Polr2a locus.
source: The newly released PC::G5-tdT mouse line provides improved functionality by targeting a Cre-dependent GCaMP5G-IRES-tdTomato transgenic cassette to the Polr2a locus (Gee et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to the paper describing the PC::G5-tdT mouse line.

claim: In the PC::G5-tdT mouse line, GCaMP5G and tdTomato are expressed individually and localize to different cell compartments.
source: However, in the PC::G5-tdT mouse line, GCaMP5G and tdTomato are expressed individually, and localize to different cell compartments.
evidence: This is a characteristic of the PC::G5-tdT design using an IRES element.

claim: In the PC::G5-tdT mouse line, tdTomato expression is driven by an internal ribosomal entry site and is highly variable and weaker than GCaMP5G.
source: Moreover, because expression of tdTomato is driven by an internal ribosomal entry site, the expression level is highly variable and weaker than GCaMP5G, limiting identification of positive cells and preventing accurate ratiometric measurements.
evidence: This is a known limitation of IRES-based expression systems.

claim: Single fluorescent protein-based indicators are problematic for Ca2+ imaging in motile cells where fluorescence changes from movement may be indistinguishable from actual changes in Ca2+ levels.
source: Although single fluorescent protein-based indicators have high brightness and fast response kinetics, as non-ratiometric probes they are problematic for Ca2+ imaging in motile cells where fluorescence changes resulting from movement may be indistinguishable from actual changes in Ca2+ levels.
evidence: This is a known limitation of non-ratiometric indicators.

claim: Salsa6f was created by fusing green GCaMP6f to the Ca2+-insensitive red fluorescent protein tdTomato.
source: Here, we introduce a novel genetically encoded Ca2+ indicator - that we christen 'Salsa6f' - by fusing green GCaMP6f to the Ca2+-insensitive red fluorescent protein tdTomato.
evidence: This describes the construction of the Salsa6f probe.

claim: Salsa6f enables true ratiometric imaging in conjunction with the high dynamic range of GCaMP6.
source: This probe enables true ratiometric imaging, in conjunction with the high dynamic range of GCaMP6.
evidence: This is a design feature and functional property of Salsa6f demonstrated in the manuscript.

claim: GCaMP6f was selected based on fluorescence intensity, dynamic range, and Ca2+ affinity suitable for detecting a spectrum of cytosolic Ca2+ signals (Kd = 375 nM).
source: We transiently expressed and screened a variety of single fluorescent protein-based GECIs in HEK 293A cells (Figure 1A), and selected GCaMP6f based on fluorescence intensity, dynamic range, and Ca2+ affinity suitable for detecting a spectrum of cytosolic Ca2+ signals (Kd = 375 nM).
evidence: This describes the selection criteria for GCaMP6f based on screening data.

claim: tdTomato was chosen for its photostability and efficient two-photon excitation.
source: To enable cell tracking even when basal Ca2+ levels evoke little GCaMP6f fluorescence, we fused GCaMP6f to the Ca2+-insensitive red fluorescent protein tdTomato, chosen for its photostability and efficient two-photon excitation (Drobizhev et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a paper characterizing tdTomato properties.

claim: A V5 epitope tag was used to link tdTomato to GCaMP6f.
source: A V5 epitope tag (Lobbestael E et al., 2010) served to link tdTomato to GCaMP6f (Figure 1B).
evidence: This describes the construction of Salsa6f with a citation for the V5 tag.

claim: Salsa6f exhibited a ten-fold dynamic range with brightness comparable to GCaMP6f alone.
source: Salsa6f exhibited a ten-fold dynamic range, with a brightness comparable to GCaMP6f alone (Figure 1A,C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A and 1C.

claim: Both components of Salsa6f can be visualized by femtosecond excitation at 900 nm for two-photon microscopy.
source: For two-photon microscopy, both components of Salsa6f can be visualized by femtosecond excitation at 900 nm (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by two-photon imaging data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: GCaMP6f produces increased green fluorescence during elevations in cytosolic Ca2+, while tdTomato provides stable red fluorescence.
source: GCaMP6f produces increased green fluorescence during elevations in cytosolic Ca2+, while tdTomato provides a stable red fluorescence that facilitates cell tracking and allows for ratiometric Ca2+ imaging (Figure 1D; Video 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by imaging data in Figure 1D and Video 1.

claim: Salsa6f is excluded from the nucleus, ensuring accurate measurement of cytosolic Ca2+ fluctuations.
source: Salsa6f is excluded from the nucleus, ensuring accurate measurement of cytosolic Ca2+ fluctuations (Figure 1D,E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by imaging data showing nuclear exclusion in Figures 1D and 1E.

claim: When expressed in human T cells, Salsa6f reported Ca2+ oscillations induced by immobilized αCD3/28 antibodies with high signal to noise ratio and time resolution.
source: When expressed by transfection in human T cells, Salsa6f reported Ca2+ oscillations induced by immobilized αCD3/28 antibodies with a high signal to noise ratio and time resolution (Figure 1E,F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data shown in Figures 1E and 1F.

claim: The Salsa6f transgenic cassette was inserted into a Gt(ROSA)26Sor5'-pCAG-FRT-LSL-Salsa6f-WPRE-bGHpA-AttB-FRT-NeoR-AttP-Gt(ROSA)26Sor3' cassette and targeted to the Rosa26 locus in JM8.N4 mouse embryonic stem (ES) cells.
source: Guided by the transgenic targeting strategy for the Ai38 mouse line (Zariwala et al., 2012), we inserted Salsa6f into a Gt(ROSA)26Sor5'-pCAG-FRT-LSL-Salsa6f-WPRE-bGHpA-AttB-FRT-NeoR-AttP-Gt(ROSA)26Sor3' cassette, then targeted it to the Rosa26 locus in JM8.N4 mouse embryonic stem (ES) cells (Figure 2A).
evidence: This describes the transgenic mouse generation strategy shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Cells positive for the Salsa6f allele were selected by neomycin resistance, and correctly targeted clones were screened by Southern blot.
source: Cells positive for the allele Gt(ROSA)26SorpCAG-FRT-LSL-Salsa6f-WPRE-bGHpA-AttB-FRT-NeoR-AttP were selected by neomycin resistance, and correctly targeted clones were screened by Southern blot (Figure 2B)
evidence: This describes the screening procedure with results shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Chimeric pups carrying the Salsa6f transgene were identified by PCR screening for the Nnt gene.
source: Chimeric pups carrying the Salsa6f transgene were identified by PCR screening for the Nnt gene, as the initial JM8.N4 ES cells were Nnt+/+ while the C57BL/6J blastocysts were Nnt-/- (Figure 2C).
evidence: This describes the screening strategy with results shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Positive chimeras were bred to R26ΦC31o mice to remove the neomycin resistance gene and produce LSL-Salsa6f F1 founders.
source: Positive chimeras were bred to R26ΦC31o mice to remove the neomycin resistance gene and to produce LSL-Salsa6f F1 founders that are heterozygotic for the Gt(ROSA)26SorpCAG-FRT-LSL-Salsa6f-WPRE-bGHpA-AttB/P allele
evidence: This describes the breeding strategy to generate the final mouse line.

claim: LSL-Salsa6f (Hom) mice were bred to Cd4Cre+/+ mice to obtain reporter mice heterozygous for Salsa6f (Cd4-Salsa6f (Het) mice) that selectively express Salsa6f in T cells.
source: LSL-Salsa6f (Hom) mice were bred to Cd4Cre+/+ mice to obtain reporter mice heterozygous for Salsa6f, designated as Cd4-Salsa6f (Het) mice from here on, that selectively express Salsa6f in T cells (Figure 3A).
evidence: This describes the breeding strategy shown in Figure 3A.

claim: 88% of Salsa6f+ cells in thymus were double positive for Cd4 and Cd8.
source: Salsa6f was detected by tdTomato fluorescence on flow cytometry. 88% of these Salsa6f+ cells in thymus were double positive for Cd4 and Cd8 (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The double-positive stage occurs during T cell development when developing thymocytes express both Cd4 and Cd8 before undergoing positive and negative selection.
source: This is due to the double-positive stage during development, in which developing thymocytes will express both Cd4 and Cd8 before undergoing positive and negative selection to become either mature Cd4+ or Cd8+ T cells.
evidence: This is established knowledge about T cell development.

claim: Salsa6f was detected in 40% of cells from spleen, 57% from lymph node, and 93% from thymus.
source: Salsa6f was readily detected by the red tdTomato signal in cells from spleen (40%), lymph node (57%), and thymus (93%) (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Double positive cells were not detected in the spleen.
source: As expected, double positive cells were not detected in the spleen (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3D and is consistent with T cell development.

claim: More than 98% of Cd4+ and Cd8+ T cells from Cd4-Salsa6f reporter mice were positive for Salsa6f.
source: More than 98% of Cd4+ and Cd8+ T cells from these reporter mice were positive for Salsa6f.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data.

claim: Salsa6f was detected in 5% of Cd19+ cells and 3% of Cd11b+ cells.
source: Salsa6f was also detected in 5% of Cd19+ cells and 3% of Cd11b+ cells (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: A small fraction of B cells express Cd4 mRNA, which may explain the presence of Salsa6f in Cd19+ cells.
source: A small fraction of B cells express Cd4 mRNA, which may explain the presence of Salsa6f in Cd19+ cells (Zhang and Henderson, 1994).
evidence: This is supported by a citation and represents a speculative explanation.

claim: Cd11b+ cells positive for Salsa6f may be splenic resident dendritic cells that also express Cd4.
source: Cd11b+ cells positive for Salsa6f may be splenic resident dendritic cells that also express Cd4 (Vremec et al., 2000; Turley et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations and represents a speculative explanation.

claim: The total number and relative frequencies of Cd4+, Cd8+, Cd19+, and Cd11b+ cells were similar between Cd4-Salsa6f mice and Cd4Cre controls.
source: The total number and relative frequencies of Cd4+, Cd8+, Cd19+, and Cd11b+ cells were similar to the Cd4Cre controls (Figure 3F,G).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figures 3F and 3G.

claim: Both heterozygotic and homozygotic Salsa6f-expressing Cd4+ T cells proliferated similar to Cd4Cre controls.
source: Both hetero and homozygotic Salsa6f-expressing Cd4+ T cells proliferated similar to the Cd4Cre controls (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This is supported by proliferation assay data shown in Figures 4A and 4B.

claim: Salsa6f-positive naive Cd4+ T cells from both Cd4-Salsa6f (Het) and Cd4-Salsa6f (Hom) mice readily differentiated into Th1, Th17, and iTreg subtypes similar to Cd4Cre controls.
source: Salsa6f-positive naive Cd4+ T cells from both Cd4-Salsa6f (Het) and Cd4-Salsa6f (Hom) mice readily differentiated into various helper T cell subtypes similar to the Cd4Cre controls (Figure 4C–E and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by differentiation assay data shown in Figures 4C-E and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Adoptively transferred Salsa6f-positive cells readily homed to lymph nodes and exhibited normal motility characteristics.
source: In addition, as described in the companion paper, adoptively transferred Salsa6f-positive cells readily homed to lymph nodes and exhibited normal motility characteristics (Dong et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by data in a companion paper.

claim: Salsa6f-expressing T lymphocytes show normal T-cell functions with respect to development, cellular phenotype, cell proliferation, differentiation, homing, and motility.
source: In summary, our results demonstrate normal T-cell functions of Salsa6f-expressing T lymphocytes with respect to development, cellular phenotype, cell proliferation, differentiation, homing, and motility.
evidence: This is a summary statement supported by multiple experimental results presented in the manuscript.

claim: Activated Cd4+ T cells expressing Salsa6f exhibited stable red fluorescence and wide fluctuations in green fluorescence due to Ca2+ oscillations resulting from T-cell receptor engagement.
source: Activated Cd4+ T cells expressing Salsa6f exhibited stable red fluorescence and wide fluctuations in green fluorescence due to Ca2+ oscillations resulting from T-cell receptor engagement (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by imaging data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Despite variability in total fluorescence between cells, the basal and peak green/red Salsa6f ratios were comparable between cells and showed up to six-fold increases during peaks in Ca2+ fluctuations.
source: Despite variability in total fluorescence between cells due to individual differences in cell size, the basal and peak green/red Salsa6f ratios (referred from now on as G/R ratio for GCaMP6f/tdTomato intensity) were comparable between cells and showed up to six-fold increases during peaks in Ca2+ fluctuations (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by imaging data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Flow cytometric analysis of Salsa6f mouse T cells revealed a 13-fold increase in G/R ratio by ionomycin treatment in Ca2+-free medium followed by Ca2+ addback.
source: Flow cytometric analysis of Salsa6f mouse T cells revealed a 13-fold increase in G/R ratio, by pretreatment with ionomycin in Ca2+-free medium to deplete cytosolic Ca2+ followed by addback of extracellular Ca2+, further emphasizing the high dynamic range of Salsa6f (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: T cells from homozygous Cd4-Salsa6f mice exhibited almost a two-fold increase in tdTomato fluorescence compared to heterozygous mice.
source: T cells from homozygous mice with two allelic copies of the Salsa6f reporter cassette exhibited almost a two-fold increase in tdTomato fluorescence compared to heterozygous mice (Figure 5E), allowing for genetic control of Salsa6f expression level when brightness is an issue.
evidence: This is demonstrated by fluorescence measurement data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Salsa6f is primarily localized to the cytoplasm and is excluded from the nucleus in naive and activated Cd4+ T cells.
source: Line scans of the confocal images of cells plated on poly-L-lysine-coated coverslips showed that Salsa6f is primarily localized to the cytoplasm and is excluded from the nucleus (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by confocal imaging and line scan data shown in Figures 6A and 6B.

claim: Increasing cytosolic Ca2+ levels using thapsigargin in 2 mM Ca2+ caused a selective increase in the GCaMP6f signal without altering the localization of Salsa6f.
source: Increasing the cytosolic Ca2+ levels using thapsigargin (TG) in 2 mM Ca2+ Ringer's solution caused a selective increase in the GCaMP6f signal, without altering the localization of Salsa6f probe.
evidence: This is demonstrated by imaging data.

claim: Small-molecule dye Ca2+ indicators fluo-4 or fura-2 loaded into Cd4+ T cells are distributed throughout the cell, including the nucleus.
source: In contrast, the small-molecule dye Ca2+ indicators fluo-4 or fura-2 loaded into Cd4+ T cells from Cd4Cre mice are distributed throughout the cell, including the nucleus (Figure 6C and data not shown).
evidence: This is demonstrated by imaging data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: In the PC::G5-tdT transgenic mouse, tdTomato is distributed throughout the cell including the nucleus while GCaMP5G is predominantly in the cytosol.
source: A different transgenic mouse, PC::G5-tdT utilizes an internal ribosomal entry site to express both tdTomato and GCaMP5G as separate proteins that localize differently (Gee et al., 2014), with tdTomato distributed throughout the cell including the nucleus and GCaMP5G predominantly in the cytosol (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by imaging data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1 and supported by a citation.

claim: In Salsa6f, both red and green fluorescent proteins are co-localized in the cytosol, allowing true ratiometric Ca2+ imaging.
source: In contrast, our tandem probe, Salsa6f, results in both red and green fluorescent proteins co-localized in the cytosol, allowing true ratiometric Ca2+ imaging and facilitating tracking of cells.
evidence: This is a design feature of Salsa6f demonstrated by imaging data.

claim: The GCaMP6f signal increased with increasing Ca2+ concentrations, but the tdTomato signal remained unchanged, suggesting minimal FRET between GCaMP6f and tdTomato.
source: We treated Salsa6f-positive T cells with Ringer's buffer containing Ionomycin and different concentrations of Ca2+ and measured the steady-state GCaMP6f and tdTomato fluorescence signals. The GCaMP6f signal increased as expected with increasing Ca2+ concentrations, but the tdTomato signal remained unchanged (Figure 6D). This suggests that the V5 epitope tag is effective in reducing FRET between GCaMP6f and tdTomato which otherwise may compromise probe performance.
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Fura-2 has an in situ Kd of approximately 225 nM at 25°C.
source: We next characterized the in situ Ca2+ affinity of Salsa6f in Cd4+ T cells isolated from Cd4-Salsa6f (Het) mice, using fura-2 as a calibration standard. Fura-2 has an in situ Kd ~225 nM at 25° C (Lewis and Cahalan, 1989)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a paper characterizing fura-2.

claim: Salsa6f responded with faster rise and decay kinetics than fura-2 to progressive increases in cytosolic Ca2+ levels, especially at lower external Ca2+ concentrations.
source: Salsa6f responded with faster rise and decay kinetics than fura-2 to progressive increases in cytosolic Ca2+ levels, especially at lower external Ca2+ concentrations.
evidence: This is demonstrated by comparative imaging experiments.

claim: Salsa6f responses saturated at lower cytosolic Ca2+ levels than fura-2 responses.
source: Salsa6f responses also saturated at lower cytosolic Ca2+ levels than fura-2 responses.
evidence: This is demonstrated by comparative imaging experiments.

claim: Genetically encoded Ca2+ indicators have been reported to have a steeper Hill coefficient than chemical indicators.
source: This is not altogether surprising given that genetically encoded Ca2+ indicators have been reported to have a steeper Hill coefficient than chemical indicators (Badura et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a paper comparing GECIs and chemical indicators.

claim: The estimated in situ Kd for Salsa6f is in the range of 160-300 nM.
source: Assuming that Cd4-Salsa6f T cells reach similar Ca2+ levels as control Cd4Cre cells, we plotted peak and the steady state G/R ratios against the cytosolic Ca2+ concentrations obtained from the fura-2 experiment which yielded an estimated in situ Kd for Salsa6f in the range of 160–300 nM (Figure 6G).
evidence: This is derived from calibration experiments shown in Figure 6G.

claim: Salsa6f is sensitive in detecting cytosolic Ca2+ from 100 nM to 2 μM, which is in the range of physiological cytosolic Ca2+ signals.
source: Based on these results, we conclude that Salsa6f is sensitive in detecting cytosolic Ca2+ from 100 nM - 2 μM, which is in the range of physiological cytosolic Ca2+ signals.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the calibration experiments and known physiological Ca2+ ranges.

claim: TCR engagement activates a canonical Ca2+ signaling pathway in T cells, characterized by IP3-induced Ca2+ release from the endoplasmic reticulum, leading to store-operated Ca2+ entry (SOCE) through Orai1 channels.
source: TCR engagement activates a canonical Ca2+ signaling pathway in T cells, characterized by IP3-induced Ca2+ release from the endoplasmic reticulum, leading to store-operated Ca2+ entry (SOCE) through Orai1 channels (Cahalan and Chandy, 2009; Prakriya and Lewis, 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge about T cell Ca2+ signaling supported by citations.

claim: Past studies on T cell Ca2+ signaling have largely relied on indicators like fura-2 and fluo-4 which have the potential drawback of being distributed into the nucleus.
source: Past studies on T cell Ca2+ signaling have largely relied on indicators like fura-2 and fluo-4 which have the potential drawback of being distributed into the nucleus, thus confounding the measurement of pure cytoplasmic Ca2+ signals, a problem particularly notable in T cells with their large nuclear to cytoplasmic volume ratio.
evidence: This is a known limitation of small molecule indicators in T cells.

claim: Salsa6f, with its high dynamic range, ratiometric readout and targeted localization in the cytosol, is well suited to record physiological cytosolic Ca2+ signals.
source: Salsa6f, with its high dynamic range, ratiometric readout and targeted localization in the cytosol, is thus well suited to record physiological cytosolic Ca2+ signals.
evidence: This is an inference based on the demonstrated properties of Salsa6f.

claim: Depleting ER Ca2+ stores with thapsigargin in Ca2+-free solution produced a small sharp initial peak indicating ER store release followed by a sustained Ca2+ signal upon restoring external Ca2+, indicative of SOCE.
source: To study SOCE more directly, we depleted ER Ca2+ stores in activated and in naïve T cells by applying TG in Ca2+-free solution. We observed a small but sharp initial peak indicating ER store release followed by a sustained Ca2+ signal upon restoring Ca2+ to the external bath, indicative of SOCE (Figure 7A, Video 3 and Figure 7—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by imaging data shown in Figure 7A, Video 3, and Figure 7—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Almost all cells responded to thapsigargin-induced SOCE.
source: Almost all cells responded to this supra-physiological stimulus (Figure 7A, right panel).
evidence: This is demonstrated by imaging data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: T cells plated on αCd3/28 showed heterogeneous responses, with some exhibiting asynchronous Ca2+ oscillations of varying frequencies and durations whereas others failed to respond.
source: In contrast, T cells plated on αCd3/28 to activate TCR-induced signaling showed heterogeneous responses, with some exhibiting asynchronous Ca2+ oscillations of varying frequencies and durations whereas others failed to respond (Figure 7B, Video 4).
evidence: This is demonstrated by imaging data shown in Figure 7B and Video 4.

claim: Ca2+ oscillations in T cells have been attributed to SOCE from repetitive opening and closing of Orai1 channels allowing Ca2+ to enter T cells in a periodic and asynchronous manner.
source: Past studies have attributed these Ca2+ oscillations to SOCE from repetitive opening and closing of Orai1 channels allowing Ca2+ to enter T cells in a periodic and asynchronous manner (Lewis and Cahalan, 1989; Dolmetsch and Lewis, 1994)
evidence: This is supported by citations to papers describing Ca2+ oscillations in T cells.

claim: Cells plated on αCd3 alone showed rhythmic oscillatory Ca2+ signals, but the percentage of responding cells was significantly lower than with αCd3/28.
source: Cells plated on αCd3 alone also showed rhythmic oscillatory Ca2+ signals; however, the percentage of responding cells was significantly lower than with αCd3/28, resulting in a lower average signal compared with αCd3/28 stimulation (Figure 7C, Video 5)
evidence: This is demonstrated by imaging data shown in Figure 7C and Video 5.

claim: Co-stimulatory signaling through Cd28 enhances the response to TCR activated Ca2+ signals.
source: These results suggest that co-stimulatory signaling through Cd28 enhances the response to TCR activated Ca2+ signals, in alignment with previous observations (Chen and Flies, 2013).
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data supported by a citation.

claim: Perfusion of external solution rapidly past T cells plated on αCd3/28-coated glass coverslips produced a transient rise in cytosolic Ca2+, likely a result of flow shear stress.
source: Finally, we focused on a novel Ca2+ signaling pathway involving mechanosensitive Ca2+-permeable channels. We examined activation of mechanosensitive channels in Salsa6f+ T cells that were plated on αCd3/28-coated glass coverslips, by flowing external solution rapidly past the cells. Perfusion produced a transient rise in the cytosolic Ca2+ signal, likely a result of flow shear stress (Figure 7D and Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by imaging data shown in Figure 7D and Figure 7—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The Piezo family of mechanosensitive channels plays a vital role in cell motility and development.
source: The Piezo family of mechanosensitive channels plays a vital role in cell motility and development (Nourse and Pathak, 2017)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a review on Piezo channels.

claim: It is not known whether Piezo channels are expressed and play a role in immune cell function.
source: but it is not known whether these channels are expressed and play a role in immune cell function.
evidence: This represents a gap in knowledge at the time of the study.

claim: Perfusion of medium including Yoda1, a selective small molecule activator of Piezo1, resulted in robust Ca2+ signals in activated and naive T cells that were larger and more sustained than those activated by perfusion of solvent or media alone.
source: Perfusion of medium including Yoda1, a selective small molecule activator of Piezo1 (Syeda et al., 2015), resulted in robust Ca2+ signals in activated and naive T cells that were larger and more sustained than those activated by perfusion of solvent or media alone (Figure 7D and Figure 7—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by imaging data shown in Figure 7D and Figure 7—figure supplement 1C, with citation for Yoda1.

claim: Salsa6f detected Ca2+ signals in T cells in response to an activator of Piezo1 channels.
source: In summary, we show Ca2+ signals in T cells in response to an activator of Piezo1 channels.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings.

claim: All subtypes of T cells (naive, Th17, iTregs) responded to plate-bound stimulation of αCd3/28 with oscillatory changes in their cytosolic Ca2+ levels, very similar to the Ca2+ responses in 2-day-activated T cells.
source: All subtypes of T cells responded to plate-bound stimulation of αCd3/28 with oscillatory changes in their cytosolic Ca2+ levels, very similar to the Ca2+ responses in 2-day-activated T cells illustrated in Figure 7B.
evidence: This is demonstrated by imaging data comparing different T cell subsets.

claim: The Ca2+ responses in different T cell subsets were heterogeneous, with some cells showing multiple peaks of varying durations and amplitudes, occasional sustained signals and other cells failing to respond.
source: The responses were heterogeneous, with some cells showing multiple peaks of varying durations and amplitudes, occasional sustained signals and other cells failing to respond.
evidence: This is demonstrated by imaging data from different T cell subsets.

claim: Some individual Th17 cells and iTregs showed higher amplitude Ca2+ signals than any naive T cells, but with a greater percentage of non-responding cells.
source: Whereas the overall average responses were not very different between the three subtypes examined, some individual Th17 cells and iTregs showed higher amplitude signals than any naive T cells, but with a greater percentage of non-responding cells.
evidence: This is demonstrated by imaging data comparing different T cell subsets.

claim: Using two-photon microscopy to image lymph nodes from Cd4-Salsa6f (Hom) mice under steady-state conditions, sporadic localized elevations of green fluorescence indicative of intracellular Ca2+ signaling were observed.
source: Using two-photon microscopy to image lymph nodes from Cd4-Salsa6f (Hom) mice under steady-state conditions, we observed sporadic localized elevations of green fluorescence indicative of intracellular Ca2+ signaling (Figure 9A,B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by two-photon imaging data shown in Figures 9A and 9B.

claim: 920 nm is the ideal two-photon excitation wavelength for simultaneous imaging of tdTomato and GCaMP6f as component parts of Salsa6f.
source: Therefore, 920 nm is the ideal two-photon excitation wavelength for simultaneous imaging of tdTomato and GCaMP6f as component parts of Salsa6f.
evidence: This conclusion is based on optimization experiments shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 1.

claim: Some of the green Salsa6f signals were T cell-sized, and the pattern of red Salsa6f fluorescence is consistent with the exclusion of the Salsa6f indicator from the nucleus.
source: Some of the green Salsa6f signals were T cell-sized, and the pattern of red Salsa6f fluorescence observed is consistent with the exclusion of the Salsa6f indicator from the nucleus (Figure 9C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by imaging data shown in Figure 9C.

claim: Numerous bright, transient green fluorescent signals termed 'sparkles' were observed, which were much smaller in area (about 2 µm2).
source: In addition, we observed numerous bright, transient green fluorescent signals which were much smaller in area (about 2 µm2 in area) (Figure 9B,D; Video 6). We term these fluorescent transients 'sparkles', because during rapid playback of time-lapse image streams cells appear to sparkle.
evidence: This is demonstrated by imaging data shown in Figures 9B, 9D, and Video 6.

claim: An image processing approach was developed to minimize fluctuations in background fluorescence and sensitively identify cell-wide Ca2+ signals and sparkles.
source: Because T cells move rapidly and are not uniformly distributed in lymph nodes, we developed an image processing approach in order to minimize fluctuations in background fluorescence and in order to sensitively identify cell-wide Ca2+ signals and sparkles (Figure 9—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This describes the image processing methodology shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 2.

claim: Based on the one-to-one correspondence of tdTomato and GCaMP6f, fluctuations in green fluorescence due to cell movement and distribution were estimated and subtracted out.
source: Based on the one-to-one correspondence of tdTomato and GCaMP6f, we estimated and subtracted out fluctuations in green fluorescence due to cell movement and distribution.
evidence: This describes the image processing approach.

claim: After processing, sparkles were found to occur widely across the imaging field.
source: After processing, sparkles were found to occur widely across the imaging field (Figure 9E–G)
evidence: This is demonstrated by processed imaging data shown in Figures 9E-G.

claim: Many sparkles reached a characteristic maximum intensity.
source: and many reached a characteristic maximum intensity (compare Figure 9F and G).
evidence: This is demonstrated by imaging data shown in Figures 9F and 9G.

claim: Hundreds of sparkle events with a mean amplitude of 6.5 SD above background were observed in each 25 min imaging session.
source: Hundreds of events with a mean amplitude of 6.5 SD above background were observed in each 25 min imaging session (one image stack every five seconds), whereas fewer than one event exceeding our threshold was expected to occur from random noise fluctuations.
evidence: This is based on statistical analysis of imaging data.

claim: Sparkles were more frequent than cell-wide transients.
source: Sparkles were more frequent than cell-wide transients (Figure 9H)
evidence: This is demonstrated by quantification shown in Figure 9H.

claim: Sparkles extended over a median area of 1.9 µm2.
source: extended over a median area of 1.9 µm2 (n = 441 sparkles from three lymph nodes; Figure 9I)
evidence: This is based on quantification of sparkle areas shown in Figure 9I.

claim: Sparkles usually lasted for only one or two consecutive frames.
source: and usually lasted for only one or two consecutive frames (Figure 9J).
evidence: This is demonstrated by temporal analysis shown in Figure 9J.

claim: Sparkle trace shape differs from that expected for autofluorescent cell processes drifting into the imaging field.
source: Sparkle trace shape differs from that expected for autofluorescent cell processes drifting into the imaging field (Figure 9K).
evidence: This is demonstrated by comparison shown in Figure 9K.

claim: Sparkles correspond to local Ca2+ signals restricted to small subcellular domains of T cells migrating through the lymph node.
source: Taken together, these observations suggest that sparkles correspond to local Ca2+ signals restricted to small subcellular domains of T cells migrating through the lymph node.
evidence: This is an inference based on the characteristics of sparkles observed in the imaging data.

claim: Small green fluorescence transients seen in lymph nodes after adoptive transfer were similar in intensity to transients seen in Cd4-Salsa6f (Hom) lymph nodes.
source: Small green fluorescence transients seen in lymph nodes after adoptive transfer were similar in intensity to transients seen in Cd4-Salsa6f (Hom) lymph nodes (Figure 10A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by comparison of imaging data shown in Figure 10A.

claim: Small, bright, and brief green fluorescence signals traced back to their origin were found in red fluorescent Cd4-Salsa6f (Hom) T cells.
source: When small, bright, and brief green fluorescence signals were traced back, they were found to originate in red fluorescent Cd4-Salsa6f (Hom) T cells (Figure 10B–M).
evidence: This is demonstrated by imaging data shown in Figures 10B-M.

claim: Some sparkles selectively localize to the front or back of motile T cells.
source: Some sparkles, identified in processed green channel images, were found to selectively localize to the front or back of motile T cells in which both the cell front and back were clearly seen (Figure 10D,E,J,K).
evidence: This is demonstrated by imaging data shown in Figures 10D, E, J, and K.

claim: Green-red channel ratiometric images confirmed differences in Ca2+ concentration between front and back of motile T cells, although regions of elevated Ca2+ were also observed flanking the nucleus.
source: Green-red channel ratiometric images, enabled by Salsa6f labeling, confirmed differences in Ca2+ concentration between front and back, although regions of elevated Ca2+ were also observed flanking the nucleus (Figure 10F,L).
evidence: This is demonstrated by ratiometric imaging data shown in Figures 10F and L.

claim: Differences in green-red channel ratiometric pixel intensities between front and back of motile T cells were highly significant (p<0.0001).
source: Differences in green-red channel ratiometric pixel intensities between front and back were highly significant (Figure 10G,M; p<0.0001, Mann–Whitney test).
evidence: This is demonstrated by statistical analysis of imaging data shown in Figures 10G and M.

claim: Motile T cells exhibit Ca2+ signals that are largely restricted to subregions of the cytoplasm.
source: Thus, motile T cells exhibit Ca2+ signals that are largely restricted to subregions of the cytoplasm, and these Ca2+ signals – sparkles – were identified with high signal-to-noise ratio by Salsa6f expression.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the imaging data showing localized Ca2+ signals.

claim: Salsa6f preserves the exceptional performance of GCaMP6f.
source: Salsa6f preserves the exceptional performance of GCaMP6f, which in the presence of high levels of Ca2+ is as bright as the standard high-performing green fluorescent protein, EGFP (Chen et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation and demonstrated by experimental data.

claim: Salsa6f possesses a dynamic range similar to GCaMP6f, and both are superior to FRET-based GECIs.
source: We find that Salsa6f possesses a dynamic range similar to GCaMP6f, and both are superior to FRET-based GECIs (Heim et al., 2007; Thestrup et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations and demonstrated by experimental data.

claim: The Ca2+ affinity of Salsa6f (160-300 nM) is well suited to detecting a variety of cellular Ca2+ signals.
source: The Ca2+ affinity of Salsa6f, 160–300 nM, is well suited to detecting a variety of cellular Ca2+ signals.
evidence: This is based on the calibration experiments and known physiological Ca2+ ranges.

claim: Inclusion of tdTomato in Salsa6f enables ratiometric imaging, calibration, and measurement of Ca2+ concentrations within cells.
source: Inclusion of tdTomato in Salsa6f enables ratiometric imaging, calibration, and measurement of Ca2+ concentrations within cells.
evidence: This is a design feature of Salsa6f demonstrated by experimental data.

claim: Salsa6f is distributed uniformly throughout the cytosol and its exclusion from the nucleus provides reliable and selective reporting of cytosolic Ca2+ signaling.
source: Moreover, Salsa6f is distributed uniformly throughout the cytosol; its exclusion from the nucleus provides reliable and selective reporting of cytosolic Ca2+ signaling.
evidence: This is demonstrated by imaging data showing cytosolic localization.

claim: A concern with any Ca2+ indicator is whether it may perturb cell function by buffering free Ca2+ ions or other means.
source: Indeed, a concern with any Ca2+ indicator is whether it may perturb cell function by buffering free Ca2+ ions or other means.
evidence: This is a general concern in the field of Ca2+ imaging.

claim: In Cd4+ immune cells, no effects of Salsa6f expression were found, even in Cd4-Salsa6f (Hom) mice, with respect to cellular phenotype, cell proliferation, differentiation, homing, and T-cell motility.
source: In Cd4+ immune cells, we found no effects of Salsa6f expression, even in Cd4-Salsa6f (Hom) mice, with respect to cellular phenotype, cell proliferation, differentiation, and, in our companion paper (Dong et al., 2017), homing and T-cell motility.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in this manuscript and a companion paper.

claim: Salsa6f was used to detect Ca2+ influx due to direct activation of SOCE, TCR stimulation, and an activator of Piezo1 channels.
source: Salsa6f was used to detect Ca2+ influx due to direct activation of SOCE, TCR stimulation, and an activator of Piezo1 channels – the latter observed in T cells for the first time to our knowledge.
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data showing Ca2+ responses to these stimuli.

claim: Differences in patterns of Ca2+ signaling were detected between naive T cells, Th17 cells, and iTregs.
source: We also detected differences in patterns of Ca2+ signaling between naive T cells, Th17 cells, and iTregs.
evidence: This is demonstrated by imaging data comparing different T cell subsets.

claim: Within tissues, nearby cells exhibit differences in morphology, connectivity, and molecular profile.
source: Within tissues, nearby cells exhibit differences, ranging from subtle to dramatic, in morphology, connectivity, and molecular profile.
evidence: This is general knowledge about tissue organization.

claim: The red fluorescence of Salsa6f, combined with genetic Salsa6f labeling, associates cellular characteristics with readout of cellular Ca2+ signaling.
source: The red fluorescence of Salsa6f, combined with genetic Salsa6f labeling, associates these characteristics with readout of cellular Ca2+ signaling.
evidence: This is an inference about the utility of Salsa6f for in vivo imaging.

claim: Both tdTomato and GCaMP6f in Salsa6f are excited well by a 920 nm femtosecond pulsed wavelength for two-photon imaging, enabling visualization hundreds of micrometers deep into lymph nodes.
source: Both the tdTomato and GCaMP6f in Salsa6f are excited well by a 920 nm femtosecond pulsed wavelength for two-photon imaging, enabling visualization hundreds of micrometers deep into lymph nodes.
evidence: This is demonstrated by two-photon imaging data.

claim: The immune system poses additional challenges for imaging because the constituent cells are highly motile.
source: The immune system poses additional challenges for imaging because the constituent cells are highly motile.
evidence: This is general knowledge about immune cell behavior.

claim: Direct cell-to-cell interactions of motile immune cells form the basis of immune surveillance.
source: Indeed, direct cell-to-cell interactions of motile immune cells form the basis of immune surveillance (Mrass et al., 2010; Krummel et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to papers on immune cell interactions.

claim: Red fluorescent Salsa6f T cells were readily identified in intact lymph nodes following adoptive transfer.
source: We were able to readily identify red fluorescent Salsa6f T cells easily in intact lymph nodes following adoptive transfer.
evidence: This is demonstrated by imaging data from adoptive transfer experiments.

claim: Salsa6f imaging revealed uniform red fluorescence labeling with clear subcellular morphology in imaging sessions encompassing hundreds of time lapse images.
source: Our images reveal uniform red fluorescence labeling by Salsa6f with clear subcellular morphology in imaging sessions encompassing hundreds of time lapse images.
evidence: This is demonstrated by time-lapse imaging data.

claim: Salsa6f offers the opportunity to record fluctuations in relative Ca2+ levels over time and to read out absolute Ca2+ concentrations within cells.
source: Moreover, Salsa6f offers the opportunity not only to record fluctuations in relative Ca2+ levels over time, but also to read out absolute Ca2+ concentrations within cells.
evidence: This is based on the ratiometric properties and calibration of Salsa6f.

claim: Knowledge of absolute Ca2+ concentrations is necessary to develop quantitative models of Ca2+ signaling and cell behavior.
source: Knowledge of absolute Ca2+ concentrations is necessary to develop quantitative models of Ca2+ signaling and cell behavior.
evidence: This is a general principle in quantitative biology.

claim: Clear Salsa6f ratio images can be generated from motile T cells in intact lymph nodes.
source: Indeed, we demonstrate that clear Salsa6f ratio images can be generated from motile T cells in intact lymph nodes.
evidence: This is demonstrated by ratiometric imaging data from lymph nodes.

claim: The Salsa6f transgenic mouse line enables more sophisticated experimental approaches including the ability to detect rare Ca2+ signaling events.
source: Our Salsa6f transgenic mouse line enables more sophisticated experimental approaches. One is the ability to detect rare Ca2+ signaling events.
evidence: This is an inference about the capabilities enabled by the Salsa6f mouse.

claim: The high brightness and dynamic range of modern GECIs like Salsa6f contribute to detection of rare Ca2+ signaling events inside intact tissues or whole transgenic animals.
source: The high brightness and dynamic range of modern GECIs like Salsa6f contribute to detection of rare Ca2+ signaling events inside intact tissues or even whole transgenic animals (Kubo et al., 2014; Portugues et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to papers demonstrating detection of rare events with GECIs.

claim: Ca2+ signals have been previously recorded within lymph nodes in adoptively transferred T cells transgenically expressing doxycycline-inducible mCameleon, GCaMP3 and dsRed as separate proteins, and virally transduced YC-nano-50CD.
source: Ca2+ signals have been previously recorded within lymph nodes in adoptively transferred T cells transgenically expressing doxycycline-inducible mCameleon (Le Borgne et al., 2016), GCaMP3 and dsRed as separate proteins (Shulman et al., 2014), and virally transduced YC-nano-50CD (Liu et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Potential disadvantages of previous Ca2+ probes used in lymph nodes include low dynamic range, nuclear expression of mCameleon and dsRed, the high Ca2+ affinity of YC-nano-50CD (50 nM), and lack of ratiometric measurement.
source: Potential disadvantages of these probes include low dynamic range, nuclear expression of mCameleon and dsRed, the high Ca2+ affinity of YC-nano-50CD (50 nM), and lack of ratiometric measurement.
evidence: This is a comparison of previous probes with Salsa6f based on known properties.

claim: Imaging T cells transgenically expressing Salsa6f helps to overcome many limitations of previous Ca2+ probes.
source: Imaging T cells transgenically expressing Salsa6f helps to overcome many of these limitations.
evidence: This is an inference based on the demonstrated properties of Salsa6f.

claim: Because of the one-to-one correspondence of tdTomato and GCaMP6f in Salsa6f, resting GCaMP6f fluorescence can be estimated and subtracted even in motile cells.
source: Because of the one-to-one correspondence of tdTomato and GCaMP6f in Salsa6f, we were able to estimate and subtract resting GCaMP6f fluorescence even in motile cells.
evidence: This describes the image processing approach enabled by Salsa6f design.

claim: The image processing approach substantially improves the uniformity of the fluorescence background upon which rare Ca2+ signaling events can be detected.
source: This approach substantially improves the uniformity of the fluorescence background upon which rare Ca2+ signaling events can be detected.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the processed imaging data.

claim: Reliable and uniform cytosolic labeling by Salsa6f contributes to detection of rare Ca2+ signaling events.
source: Reliable and uniform cytosolic labeling contributes as well.
evidence: This is an inference about how Salsa6f properties contribute to event detection.

claim: The sensitivity and resolution of Salsa6f images are sufficient to map local Ca2+ signals from intact lymph nodes to sub-regions of T cells.
source: The sensitivity and resolution of these images are sufficient to map local signals from intact lymph nodes to sub-regions of T cells.
evidence: This is demonstrated by imaging data showing subcellular localization of Ca2+ signals.

claim: While the study focused on the brightest local Ca2+ signals to demonstrate their existence, Salsa6f is expected to enable detection of even lower intensity Ca2+ signals.
source: Moreover, while we focused upon the brightest local Ca2+ signals to demonstrate their existence, we expect that Salsa6f will enable even lower intensity Ca2+ signals to be linked to subcellular mechanisms and, ultimately, resulting cell behaviors.
evidence: This is a speculation about future capabilities of Salsa6f.
